a word used to. denote compassion, or pity, and admiration of one's beauty; (M, K;) the object being a child; (K;) as when one says of a child, wayosahu maA A^amolaHahu [ Merry on him! or the like: how beautiful is he! ]: (TA:) or wayosN and wayoHN are used in the place of wayolN ; (TA;) and wayosN lahu signifies wayolN lahu [ Woe to him! ]: (M, TA:) or, as some say, wayosN is a word denoting contempt; and has no verb; analogy forbidding that it should have one: (IJ, M:) Aboo-Turáb says, I heard Abu-sSemeyda' say, wayosN and wayoHN and wayolN have one meaning: (TA:) or wayosaka is not said except to children; and wayolaka is an expression in which is roughness and reproach; and wyH is a gentle and good expression.
